title: Java Class Methods
learningObjectives: Declare instance methods inside a class.
Call an instance method through an object reference.
Use this to refer to the current object when appropriate.
Distinguish instance methods from static methods.
Explain how methods can read and update an object's fields.

understand.concept: A class method defines behaviour associated with a class. An instance method operates on a particular object and can use its instance fields. A static method belongs to the class and cannot directly use instance members without an object reference.
understand.whyItMatters: Methods keep operations close to the data they manage. They allow objects to expose useful behaviour while keeping implementation details inside the class.
understand.analogy: Think of a well-designed object as a small service with a clear responsibility: it keeps the information it owns and exposes only the operations other code needs.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy is only a design aid; Java access, inheritance and dispatch follow the language's exact rules.

explain.narrative:
## Instance methods

Declare methods inside a class. Call an instance method through an object reference. The method can read or update that object's fields.

## The this reference

Inside an instance method or constructor, `this` refers to the current object. It is often used to distinguish a field from a parameter with the same name.

## Static methods

A static method belongs to the class. It can be called with the class name and cannot use `this` or access instance fields directly.

## Common mistakes

- Calling an instance method directly from a static context.
- Using `this` inside a static method.
- Confusing a method declaration with a method call.

examples.title: Call an instance method
examples.code:
class Message { void show() { System.out.println("Ready"); } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Message m = new Message(); m.show(); } }
examples.explanation: The method is called on the Message object.

examples.title: Method updates an object's field
examples.code:
class Score { int points; void add(int value) { points += value; } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Score s = new Score(); s.add(6); s.add(4); System.out.println(s.points); } }
examples.explanation: The instance method changes the state of the object it belongs to.

examples.title: Use this for the current object
examples.code:
class User { String name; void setName(String name) { this.name = name; } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { User u = new User(); u.setName("Ravi"); System.out.println(u.name); } }
examples.explanation: this.name refers to the field; name refers to the parameter.

examples.title: A static method belongs to the class
examples.code:
class Calculator { static int doubleValue(int n) { return n * 2; } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println(Calculator.doubleValue(7)); } }
examples.explanation: A static method can be called using the class name.

examples.title: Two objects keep separate method state
examples.code:
class Lamp { int level; void setLevel(int n) { level = n; } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Lamp a = new Lamp(); Lamp b = new Lamp(); a.setLevel(2); b.setLevel(5); System.out.println(a.level + ":" + b.level); } }
examples.explanation: Each instance method call updates the object used for that call.

questions.prompt: How is an instance method usually called?
questions.explanation: An instance method is invoked on an object.
this is a reference to the current instance.

questions.prompt: Can a static method directly access an instance field without an object?
options: Only when the field is private
questions.explanation: Static methods have no current instance and need an object reference.
The static modifier appears before the return type.

questions.prompt: Why place behaviour in a class method?
questions.answer: To keep operations associated with the data they manage
options: To keep operations associated with the data they manage
questions.explanation: Methods encapsulate behaviour with the class's state.
